name: AL-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans 17 points Republican, making an upset historically unlikely
Jerry Carl holds a roughly 13-to-1 fundraising edge plus $547,000 in outside support
Prediction markets price the Republican near 94%
No polls or expert ratings cover the open-seat race
model.rationale: An R+17 open district, a lopsided money advantage for Jerry Carl, and markets pricing him around 94% all point the same way, and no polling suggests competition. The race stays Safe Republican with an expected margin in the mid-teens.
model.watch: Late Democratic outside spending, fresh polling, or a major Republican misstep could narrow the outlook, though the district's lean leaves little room for an upset.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's 1st District is an open seat, and Republicans enter as heavy favorites in a district that leaned 17 points toward them at the presidential level. Republican Jerry Carl has raised about $1.16 million and holds $367,000 on hand, with outside groups adding roughly $547,000 in support on his side. Democrat Clyde Jones Jr. has raised about $86,000 with $28,000 available.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put Republican odds around 94%. With the money gap this wide and the district this red, the seat rates as Safe Republican; the open question is the size of the margin, not the winner.
